title: Google Photos just halved the time you have to rescue trashed pictures
summary: Google Photos is starting to clear your trash after 30 days, not 60.
body: TL;DR Last month we spotted Google Photos preparing to implement a new 30-day retention limit on deleted pics. A few days ago, Google updated its Photos support docs to reference the new 30-day policy. Now Android users are also starting to get notifications within the app. How much effort do you put into to curating your photographs? When you’ve got a giant bucket of Google One storage to fill up, some users will just save every snapshot they ever take. Even when you have all the space in the world, there’s a lot to be said for weeding out the pics you definitely don’t want. But what if you end up second-guessing yourself? Maybe that questionable pic is worth keeping, after all? Hopefully you make up your mind soon, because Google Photos is slashing your restore window in half for trashed pics. So far, if you’ve backed up an image with Google Photos, then moved that pic to the trash, you’d get a 60-day grace period before it was deleted for good. For pics that are just stored locally on a device, you’ve only had 30 days.

title: GrapheneOS is building its own RCS support to cut Google Messages out of the picture
summary: The privacy-focused OS is also redesigning Messaging app and rethinking clipboard access.
body: TL;DR GrapheneOS is overhauling its Messaging app with a redesigned interface, improvements, and bug fixes. RCS support is coming to GrapheneOS’ own Messaging app, eventually reducing its reliance on Google Messages. summary: Action Notch changed the way I do so many things on my phone.
body: Like everyone else, I install a bunch of apps after setting up a new Android phone. Some of these are essentials like Bitwarden and Ente Auth, while others are productivity apps I can’t live without . It doesn’t end there, though. I also use a few utility apps that are among the first apps to go on my phone. On Pixel phones, it’s the Essentials app , which unlocks a ton of new functionality. And for all the other Android phones I test, I can’t live without Action Notch — a free Android app that helps me get the most out of my phone’s notch.

summary: These two basic features are available on this new mid-ranger and its predecessors, but not on the Pixel 11.
body: Credit: Hadlee Simons / Android Authority Google launched the Pixel 11 series a little under a month ago, and there’s a lot to like here. All four phones offer more capable silicon, nifty AI tricks, some cool camera features, and a lengthy software update policy. Unfortunately, the standard Pixel 11 lacks many camera features compared to the Pixel 11 Pro series. And a brand new $500 Android phone from a rival manufacturer drives home just how absurd Google’s practice around this continues to be.

title: Motorola and Google foldables are quietly beating Samsung where it counts
summary: Samsung forgot the foldable features that truly matter.
body: If you need a foldable with the best specs and budget isn’t a factor, the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra takes the crown. It isn’t even really that close. With its thin-and-light form factor, 5,000mAh silicon-carbon battery, Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 for Galaxy chip , and standout rear camera system, the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra is arguably the flagship foldable with the fewest compromises. So why don’t I want to use it? I’ve tried every book-style foldable released in the US this year, and if I ranked them in the order of most likely to earn a spot in my pocket, the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra would come in last. I’d pick both the Motorola Razr Fold and the Google Pixel 11 Pro Fold over it, despite their weaker performance and hardware drawbacks. I’d even go with the wide Galaxy Z Fold 8 over the Ultra model, accepting its limitations.

title: The best Android alarm app isn’t on the Play Store. Here’s how to install it
summary: This Clock app isn't on the Play Store, but that doesn't mean it isn't worth getting!
body: Credit: Andy Walker / Android Authority Most people stick to the defaults when it comes to apps like your calendar, texting app, and clock. The reality is that plenty of third-party apps do the job better, and Chrono is one of them. Far from a household name, Chrono is an open-source clock app that puts both Samsung and Google’s default Clock apps to shame. It has a great UI, plenty of useful alarm features, and no ads. It’s also easy to overlook because it isn’t officially available on the Google Play Store.

title: This RO water filter has earned a permanent spot next to my desk
summary: It's never been this easy to stay hydrated!
body: Think about it: Water is among the most important things for humans, only second to oxygen. Without it, we can’t live for more than a few days. Needless to say, it’s an important part of your everyday life, so why not invest in good drinking water? Sure, you can buy purified water, but it gets expensive over time, not to mention the time and trips to the store. Then, there are the complicated filtration systems that can be installed under the sink, but those are also mighty pricey, hard to install, and often not even a viable option for renters.

title: I want better Samsung phones, but these new sales numbers show why we won’t get them

But that idea has seemed increasingly nostalgic as competitors in other markets overtake the company’s smartphones when it comes to hardware specs. Sometimes, even budget and mid-range devices have features that make Samsung’s phones seem outdated in comparison. Despite the yearning among many for Samsung to return to its history of innovation, that’s unlikely to happen anytime soon. And the key reason lies in its sales.

summary: The hardware makes the case. NXTPAPER sweetens the deal.
body: Credit: Paul Jones / Android Authority The most compelling phones don’t make you choose between strong everyday hardware and something genuinely different. Unique features can add plenty to the experience, but they don’t paper over the cracks if you’re not getting the specs your money deserves. TCL’s new P80 Series arrives this month with the specs to back up its headline features. The P80 Ultra leads the range with hardware that compares strongly with rivals in the same price range, making a strong case for the P80 Series as one of the best-value smartphone options in its segment. At IFA 2026 in Berlin, Blurams is presenting a lineup that promises complete, thorough coverage and includes everything from solar-powered outdoor cameras to indoor domes, a local storage hub, and even an AI companion toy for kids. title: The new W4 Plus is Timekettle’s most capable AI interpreter earbuds yet
summary: Whether for travel or at work, you can now cross the language barrier with ease.
body: Credit: Timekettle Whether you’re dealing with a menu you can’t read, figuring out road signs, or asking someone for directions, the translation tools on our phones are undoubtedly helpful. The use case is rather narrow, though, and these apps aren’t up to the task if you’re in a meeting, on a call, or just trying to have a regular conversation with someone across a language gap. That’s what the Timekettle W4 Plus is for. Timekettle’s latest pair of AI interpreter earbuds is built for two-way, face-to-face conversation and makes it feel natural at every stage. You wear one earbud, the person you’re talking to wears the other, and you each just talk. No one has to hold a phone between you and wait for a translator app to catch up. The W4 Plus and the Timekettle’s latest software package are making their debut here at IFA 2026. Here’s what you need to know.

title: I thought losing Flex Mode would ruin the Galaxy Z Fold 8 — I was completely wrong
summary: Samsung's new hinge really does make up for it.
body: When I first heard of Samsung’s plans to make a wide Galaxy Z Fold 8 , I knew I’d want one in my pocket. The 16:10 cover screen and 4:3 main screen aspect ratios sounded perfect for widescreen content consumption, and made for a compact form factor when shut. Before I bought a Galaxy Z Fold 8 for myself, I skimmed the spec sheet and looked for any notable downgrades. Neither the slightly smaller battery nor the rear dual-camera system disappointed me, but the lack of Flex Mode initially stunned me. Flex Mode allows you to prop up a foldable like a laptop. It uses a mix of hardware that keeps the hinge in a fixed position and software that makes the most of the split-screen UI. I’ve been using Flex Mode on Samsung foldables since the Galaxy Z Flip 3, and it became my preferred way to watch videos on a table or desk.

body: A lot has been said about the Pixel 11 Pro and 11 Pro XL since their unveiling on August 12 — much of it not very good. Pixel phones always come with an extra heaping of criticism, warranted or not, but there are real concerns about this year’s Pro phones. They have less RAM than last year’s models, HiLight has already proven disappointing , the Tensor G6 chip isn’t a particularly big performance upgrade , and the phones are more expensive than ever before. Considering all that, it would be safe to assume the Pixel 11 Pro () and Pixel 11 Pro XL () aren’t good phones. However, after spending about three weeks with both of them, I don’t think that could be further from the truth.

summary: Google has some catching up to do.
body: Credit: Robert Triggs / Android Authority I switch phones for a living, so I don’t say this lightly: Google makes great phones. But “great” and “the phone I’d actually buy and recommend to friends” are two very different things. I’ve used Galaxy and Pixel phones for years, and I always come back to a Galaxy. And no, this has nothing to do with foldables, the S Pen, or any of that stuff that only matters to a small group of users. It’s because of the experience that actually counts when you’re living with the same device for two or three years. Samsung just gets more of that right, at least for me. The Pixel 11 lineup hasn’t changed that.

summary: Original Chromecasts still beat Google TV for simple streaming.
body: Credit: Robert Triggs / Android Authority News that the original Chromecast has just received an unexpected update is music to my ears. I’m a big fan of the simplicity of those early HDMI dongles, far more than I am of the overly verbose and often laggy Google TV . I suppose I’m still just attached to my earliest smart TV experience, flinging content at my TV from my phone rather than running the gauntlet of advertisements just to find my favorite show. If it ain’t broken, don’t fix it, as they say, and my Chromecast (3rd gen) still sees occasional use. In fact, I’ve been using it a lot more in the past couple of years to placate two impatient youngsters.

title: Google Photos on Android just got an iPhone feature I’ve waited a year for — how to use it now
summary: Manual! Photo! Stacks! Are! Here!
body: In May 2025, the Google Photos app got an incredible feature: the ability to manually create photo stacks . Google Photos has long automatically created stacks of similar-looking pictures, helping to better organize your library. However, that automated process doesn’t always work as you’d like, leaving your Photos library more chaotic than you’d prefer. Manual stacking fixes that issue perfectly — but there’s been just one problem: it’s been exclusive to the Photos app on iOS . There’s been evidence of manual stacking coming to the Android app for a while, but month after month, it’s remained MIA.

title: 5 Android apps you should use instead of Google Keep
summary: There are better ways to keep notes than Keep.
body: Google Keep is a popular note-taking app, especially among those looking for a simple app for quick note-taking. It’s free, lightweight, and easy to use. Plus, it automatically syncs your notes across all devices at no extra cost and without additional configuration. Having said that, Google Keep has its own share of limitations. Jackson NASA Headquarters building in Washington NASA/Joel Kowsky On Wednesday, June 17, skywatchers across the United States—and parts of Canada—enjoyed a rare event: a daytime lunar occultation of Venus. A lunar occultation occurs when the Moon moves directly in front of another celestial object from our viewpoint on Earth, briefly hiding it from sight. This time, the Moon slipped in front of Venus for the first of three occultations happening this year, creating a striking daylight moment for those who caught it.
